COMM 101.description: Concepts and processes relevant to the study of communication and human behavior and their application in a broad variety of contexts, including interpersonal relationships, small groups, organizations, health communication, social media, and media literacy.
COMM 101.subject: COMM
COMM 101.title: Introduction to Human Communication

COMM 201.description: Focus on skills development in goal oriented two person conversations. Topics include an overview of the communication process in employment interviews, informational interviews, survey interviews, performance appraisals; recruiting interviews, persuasive interviews; counseling and health care interviews.
COMM 201.subject: COMM
COMM 201.title: Applied Interpersonal Communication

COMM 202.description: Introduction to theoretical and applied issues in interpersonal persuasion and persuasion campaigns. Presents an overview of the area with an emphasis on critical analysis about the creation and consumption of persuasive messages.
COMM 202.subject: COMM
COMM 202.title: Social Influence and Persuasion

COMM 203.description: Introduction to the theoretical and applied issues to how individuals communicate in teams, how teams are created and defined through communication, and how teams communicate with other teams across organizations. Crucial to understanding and strengthening future teamwork experiences in organizations.
COMM 203.subject: COMM
COMM 203.title: Communication in Teams

COMM 204.description: Surveys a range of conflict settings, including communication in interpersonal, group, and organizational contexts. Focuses on the application of theory and research to help students develop the skills needed to manage conflict effectively in their personal and professional lives.
COMM 204.subject: COMM
COMM 204.title: Conflict and Negotiation

COMM 308.description: A developmental approach to media uses and effects research, considering cognitive, emotional, and social development as a framework for thinking about media effects on youth.
COMM 308.subject: COMM
COMM 308.title: Media and Youth

COMM 310.description: Presents a comprehensive introduction to nonverbal communication. Covers the evolutionary and socio-cultural foundations as well as the basic codes and functions of nonverbal communication as well as the applications of nonverbal communication concepts to everyday interactions.
COMM 310.subject: COMM
COMM 310.title: Nonverbal Communication

COMM 312.description: Examines how gender influences communication and the multiple relationships among gender, communication and culture. Explores how communication creates gender and shapes relationships and how communication reflects, sustains, and alters cultural views of gender.
COMM 312.subject: COMM
COMM 312.title: Gender and Communication

COMM 332.description: Fundamentals of communications research methods and applications. Survey, observational and experimental research; primary research data-gathering techniques; secondary research sources; concept of data analysis; message and audience research measures.
COMM 332.subject: COMM
COMM 332.title: Communication Research

COMM 336.description: Introduction to crisis communications and management from a strategic, theory-based approach using research from historical and current case studies.
COMM 336.subject: COMM
COMM 336.title: Crisis Communications

COMM 399.description: Supervised communications research experience to develop student’s advanced research and analytical skills. Individual research contract developed in consultation with the instructor.
COMM 399.subject: COMM
COMM 399.title: Research Experience in Communication

COMM 406.description: Development of critical thinking skills for analyzing mass media.
COMM 406.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in JOUR 101.
COMM 406.subject: COMM
COMM 406.title: Mass Media Criticism

COMM 425.description: An introduction to research trends and theory in the scientific study of the family, considering issues related to family interaction, functioning, relationships, and communication.
COMM 425.subject: COMM
COMM 425.title: Family Communication

COMM 426.description: Survey of concepts, theories, and research concerning communication across all phases of interpersonal relationships, focusing on both theoretical and practical applications.
COMM 426.subject: COMM
COMM 426.title: Communication in Social and Personal Relationships

COMM 435.description: Explores the diversity of health experiences and the ways in which health communication affects our lives, whether through interpersonal conversations about health issues, exposure to health information in the media, or through our personal involvement with the healthcare system.
COMM 435.subject: COMM
COMM 435.title: Health Communication

COMM 436.description: Survey of the theoretical and empirical literature dealing with human communication behavior as it occurs within the context of complex organizations. Among the topics covered are superior-subordinate communication, communication networks, message distortion, feedback processes, communication climate, leadership and decision-making.
COMM 436.subject: COMM
COMM 436.title: Communication in Complex Organizations

COMM 499.description: Topics in communication and media effects. Individual topics will vary by title.
COMM 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in COMM 332.
COMM 499.subject: COMM
COMM 499.title: Special Topics in the Scientific Approach to Media Effects

COMM 507.description: Explores the role of journalism in shaping perceptions of scientific issues and task. Emphasis on methods of effectively communicating about science, health, and the environment.
COMM 507.subject: COMM
COMM 507.title: Health Communication: The Science and Practice

COMM 509.description: The role of journalism in shaping perceptions of environmental and scientific issues and tasks. Emphasis on methods of effectively communicating about science and the environment.
COMM 509.subject: COMM
COMM 509.title: Environmental Communication: The Science and Practice

COMM 542.description: Theory and practice of persuasive communication and the role of persuasion in shaping public opinion.
COMM 542.subject: COMM
COMM 542.title: Public Opinion and Persuasion

COMM 562.description: Examines how people form their identities and manage their personal relationships using new communication technologies (social network sites, online dating, mobile computing, video games). Topics include impression management, deception and trust, self-perception and identity, social support and relationship maintenance.
COMM 562.subject: COMM
COMM 562.title: Online Communication and Personal Relationships

COMM 572.description: The relation of communication processes to interethnic and interracial attitudes and behavior. Psycho-social foundations of interethnic communication and conflict, group identification and communication processes, interpersonal communication and culture, communication about race and ethnicity, mass media content and effects.
COMM 572.subject: COMM
COMM 572.title: Communication and Interethnic Behavior

COMM 596.description: Study abroad course will focus on topics in journalism and mass communications and will be taught as a study abroad experience. Individual topics will vary by title.
COMM 596.subject: COMM
COMM 596.title: Study Abroad in Journalism and Mass Communications
